title: Bowery party costumes and the band members in the photo
summary: The casual attire was a Bowery party theme; Rau identifies Benji White, Monk Smith and Dick, noting the band was a string band before the saxophonists.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: And I was wondering about the attire that you were wearing at the Chess and Checkers Club. It was very casual.
Well, it was a Bowery party. That's what they called it.
So it was a special occasion, a special theme of some kind.

Yeah. They gave it a name, and everybody was dressed up in raggedy clothes, anything they could think of. You know, for the, I don't know, I think it was a stick, I mean, a red hat on a big derby, if I'm not mistaken. And a cigar on his mouth.
Yeah. And Benji White had a black eye, it looks like. That's right. Yeah.
Did you ever see that? Yeah. That's funny. And Monk Smith had a stupid look in his face. He was on the front row.
And my dad had his eyes closed for some reason. He was only a real kid then, and I think he must have been 16 years old.

Yeah, I think Dick had just started playing with us then. He didn't come into the picture until a few years after we got started. But up until that time we were more or less a string band. We didn't have a couple of saxophone players. That was Benji White and Monk Smith.
Well he was originally a guitarist with the string group, wasn't he?
